## Overview

This interactive companion site accompanies the paper:

> **Skill, Sequence, and Scoring: A Mathematical Comparison of Traditional and World Bowling Scoring Systems**
>
> Michael Borck, Curtin University

The paper demonstrates that traditional ten-pin bowling scoring and the World Bowling current-frame system differ in mathematically precise and practically significant ways.

## Key Findings

### 1. Traditional scoring is sequence-sensitive

The order of frames matters. The same frame composition can produce a score range of **up to 39 points** under traditional scoring, while World Bowling collapses all orderings to a single score.

**[Try it yourself &rarr;](explorer.qmd)**

### 2. Traditional scoring has a compounding reward gradient

Each consecutive strike is worth more than the last. Under World Bowling, every strike is worth the same regardless of context.

**[Explore the gradient &rarr;](reward.qmd)**

### 3. The crossover point is ~50% strike rate

Below 50% strike rate, World Bowling provides more score spread. Above it, traditional scoring provides **33% more spread** at the professional level.

### 4. Within-tier discrimination matters most

Both systems separate recreational from professional players equally well. The critical difference is in separating two elite players who differ in their ability to sustain consecutive strikes.

## Reproducibility

All code, data, and figures are available at:

- **Source code**: [github.com/michael-borck/skill-sequence-scoring](https://github.com/michael-borck/skill-sequence-scoring)

To reproduce all results:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/michael-borck/skill-sequence-scoring.git
cd skill-sequence-scoring
pip install -r requirements.txt
cd src
python bowling_distributions.py    # Exact score distributions
python bowling_analysis.py         # Sequence sensitivity analysis
python bowling_simulation.py       # Monte Carlo simulation
python bowling_visualisations.py   # Generate figures 1-5
python sequence_permutations.py    # Exhaustive permutation analysis
python simulation_figures.py       # Generate figures 8-11
```
